newsitem.title: USA: Glickman sees US 1997 beef exports rising sharply.
newsitem.headline: Glickman sees US 1997 beef exports rising sharply.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said he expected U.S. beef exports to rise sharply this year as world markets open up.
"With strong economic growth in 1997 we expect beef exports to resume the record growth of the 1990s," he said at the National Cattlemen's Beef Association annual convention.
"The key to the future of American agriculture and the key to the future of the livestock industry is opening world markets," Glickman said.
"That (the rest of the world) is where the population growth is, that is where the economic growth is and that is where increased income comes from," he added.
He noted that 1997 could be the year when China finally enters the World Trade Organization (WTO).
"As a sign of good faith China should start bringing down their barriers now, and not just for CDs and stereos but for beef and other agricultural products as well," he said.

Glickman also referred to the dispute with the European Union on the EU's ban on the import of meat products treated with growth hormones. The ban has been in place since 1989 and has prevented an estimated $100 million in U.S. beef sales each year.
A WTO panel has been formed to settle the dispute.
"Study after scientific study has shown that this beef to be perfectly safe. If the WTO decision is based on sound science we will see this unfair policy reversed" he said.
The U.S. Meat Export Federation earlier this week set an export goal for U.S. beef and beef variety meats in 1997 of 1.17 million tonnes, up from 982,000 tonnes in 1996.
